chunks: 3049 - And it is narrated from Dāwūd al-Raqqī, who said:
One of the Khawārij asked me about this verse from the Book of Allah, the Exalted,
"Eight pairs: of sheep two, and of goats two."
up to His, the Exalted, saying:
"And of camels two, and of cattle two."

What is it from that which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made halal, and what is it that He has forbidden? I had nothing with me regarding it, so I entered upon Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while I was a pilgrim, and I informed him of what had happened. He said:

"Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has permitted in the sacrificial offering at Minā the domesticated sheep and goats, and He has forbidden that the mountain species be offered there in sacrifice. As for His saying, Mighty and Majestic,
"And of camels two, and of cattle two,"

then indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has permitted in the sacrificial offering at Minā the Arabian camels, and He has forbidden in it the Bactrian camels; and He has permitted the domesticated cattle to be offered in sacrifice, and He has forbidden the mountain species."
So I went back to the man and informed him of this answer, and he said: "This is something the camels have carried from the Ḥijāz."

key_terms.الْآيَةِ: the Qur'anic verse being asked about
key_terms.الْأَهْلِيَّةَ: domesticated animals that are permitted here for sacrifice
key_terms.الْأُضْحِيَّةِ: the sacrificial offering performed at Minā
key_terms.الْبَخَاتِيَّ: Bactrian camels excluded here from sacrificial validity
key_terms.الْجَبَلِيَّةَ: wild or mountain-dwelling species that are not permitted here for sacrifice
key_terms.الْعِرَابَ: Arabian camels considered valid here for sacrifice
key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Minā, the location connected to hajj sacrifice

ai.seo_question: Which animals are permitted for sacrificial offering at Minā according to this verse and hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic mention of livestock by clarifying which animals are valid for sacrificial offering at Minā. It distinguishes between domesticated and certain wild or non-standard species, showing the Imam's role in explaining legal meanings found in the Qur'an.
